questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The Cahn-Ingold-Prelog (CIP) absolute configuration of 2-hydroxypropanoic acid drawn in a Fischer projection with $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ at the top, $-\text{CH}_3$ at the bottom, $-\text{OH}$ on the right, and $-\text{H}$ on the left is:
questions.explanationEn: At C2 of 2-hydroxypropanoic acid, the CIP priority order is $-\text{OH}$ (1) $> -\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ (2) $> -\text{CH}_3$ (3) $> -\text{H}$ (4). Tracing $1 \to 2 \to 3$ goes from right (3 o'clock) to top (12 o'clock) to bottom (6 o'clock), which is counter-clockwise. Because the lowest-priority group $-\text{H}$ lies on a horizontal bond (pointing toward the viewer in a Fischer projection), the result is reversed to $(R)$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Nucleophilic addition of $\text{HCN}$ to acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) exclusively from its $Re$ face produces:
optionsEn: $(S)$-2-hydroxypropanenitrile
$(R)$-2-hydroxypropanenitrile
A racemic mixture of 2-hydroxypropanenitrile
An achiral cyanohydrin
questions.explanationEn: At the carbonyl carbon of acetaldehyde, CIP priorities are $=\text{O}$ (1) $> -\text{CH}_3$ (2) $> -\text{H}$ (3). On the $Re$ face, $1 \to 2 \to 3$ proceeds clockwise (e.g., $\text{O}$ at $+y$, $\text{CH}_3$ at $+x/-y$, $\text{H}$ at $-x/-y$). Attack by $\text{CN}^-$ from the $+z$ ($Re$) face creates a stereocenter with priorities $-\text{OH}$ (1) $> -\text{CN}$ (2) $> -\text{CH}_3$ (3) $> -\text{H}$ (4). Viewing along the $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond from $\text{C}$ to $\text{H}$ places $1 \to 2 \to 3$ ($-\text{OH} \to -\text{CN} \to -\text{CH}_3$) in a counter-clockwise sense, giving $(S)$-2-hydroxypropanenitrile.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The preference of 2-methoxytetrahydropyran to place the C2 methoxy group in the axial rather than the equatorial orientation (the endo-anomeric effect) is best explained by:
optionsEn: Steric attraction between the axial methoxy group and the C4/C6 axial hydrogens
Hyperconjugative overlap between the axial lone pair of the ring oxygen ($n_{\text{O}}$) and the antiperiplanar $\sigma^*_{\text{C2}-\text{OMe}}$ orbital
Hyperconjugative overlap between the equatorial lone pair of the ring oxygen and the $\sigma^*_{\text{C2}-\text{H}}$ orbital
Intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the methoxy oxygen and the C6 methylene protons
questions.explanationEn: In 2-methoxytetrahydropyran, when the C2 $-\text{OMe}$ group is axial, its $\text{C2}-\text{OMe}$ bond is antiperiplanar ($180^\circ$) to one of the lone pairs ($n_{\text{O}}$) on the endocyclic ring oxygen. This geometry enables stabilizing $n_{\text{O}} \to \sigma^*_{\text{C2}-\text{OMe}}$ hyperconjugation (and also minimizes dipole-dipole repulsion), favoring the axial conformer.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a Hammett linear free-energy relationship $\log(k_X/k_H) = \rho \sigma_X$, a reaction exhibiting a large POSITIVE reaction constant ($\rho = +2.8$) indicates that:
optionsEn: Positive charge develops at the reaction center in the rate-determining transition state
Negative charge develops at the reaction center in the rate-determining transition state
The reaction proceeds via a radical intermediate with no charge development
Electron-donating substituents accelerate the reaction rate
questions.explanationEn: Because electron-withdrawing substituents have positive $\sigma_X$ values, a positive reaction constant ($\rho > 0$) means that electron-withdrawing groups increase the rate ($k_X > k_H$). This occurs when negative charge builds up (or positive charge is depleted) at or adjacent to the reaction center in the rate-determining transition state, and the large magnitude ($+2.8$) reflects high sensitivity to substituent electronic effects.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The solvolysis of *anti*-7-norbornenyl tosylate in acetic acid is approximately $10^{11}$ times faster than that of saturated 7-norbornyl tosylate. This extraordinary rate acceleration is due to:
optionsEn: Steric relief of the $\text{C}2=\text{C}3$ double bond
Anchimeric assistance (neighboring group participation) by the $\pi$-electrons of the $\text{C}2=\text{C}3$ double bond forming a symmetric non-classical bishomocyclopropenyl cation
Direct $E2$ elimination facilitated by the double bond
Inductive electron donation from the $sp^2$ hybridized carbons
questions.explanationEn: In *anti*-7-norbornenyl tosylate, the $\text{C}2=\text{C}3$ $\pi$-bond is ideally oriented antiperiplanar to the departing C7-$\text{OTs}$ bond. Backside $\pi$-participation assists ionization to form a highly delocalized, symmetric $2\pi$-electron bishomocyclopropenyl non-classical cation, accelerating solvolysis by a factor of $\sim 10^{11}$ and giving complete retention of configuration.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following molecules are CHIRAL (optically active)?
optionsEn: 1,3-Dimethylallene ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3$)
*trans*-1,2-Dichlorocyclopropane
*cis*-1,3-Dimethylcyclohexane
2,6-Dimethylspiro[3.3]heptane
questions.explanationEn: (A) 1,3-Dimethylallene has orthogonal terminal planes with two different groups ($\text{H}, \text{Me}$) on each end ($C_2$ symmetry), so it is axially chiral. (B) *trans*-1,2-Dichlorocyclopropane has $C_2$ symmetry with no $\sigma$ plane or $i$, so it is chiral. (C) *cis*-1,3-Dimethylcyclohexane has a mirror plane passing through C2 and C5, making it an achiral *meso* compound. (D) 2,6-Dimethylspiro[3.3]heptane has two mutually perpendicular rings with $\text{H} \neq \text{Me}$ at C2 and C6 ($C_2$ symmetry), making it axially chiral. Hence, (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following species are **aromatic**?
optionsEn: Azulene ($\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_8$)
Cyclooctatetraenyl dianion ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_8^{2-}$)
Borazine ($\text{B}_3\text{N}_3\text{H}_6$)
Pentalene ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_6$)
questions.explanationEn: (A) Azulene is a planar bicyclic $10\,\pi$-electron ($4(2)+2$) aromatic hydrocarbon with a substantial dipole moment. (B) Cyclooctatetraenyl dianion ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_8^{2-}$) is planar and has $10\,\pi$ electrons, making it aromatic. (C) Borazine is a planar $6\,\pi$-electron inorganic analogue of benzene with aromatic delocalization. (D) Pentalene has $8\,\pi$ electrons ($4n$) and is antiaromatic. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about reactive intermediates are CORRECT?
optionsEn: A carbon-centered radical bearing both an electron-donating group and an electron-withdrawing group (captodative effect) enjoys enhanced stabilization
Singlet dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$) is lower in energy than triplet dichlorocarbene due to $\pi$-donation from the chlorine lone pairs into the empty carbene $p$-orbital
The parent methyl radical ($^{\bullet}\text{CH}_3$) is strongly pyramidal with an $\text{H}-\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond angle of $104.5^\circ$
Acylium ions ($\text{R}-\text{C}\equiv\text{O}^+$) are linear and resonance-stabilized by an oxygen lone pair
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Simultaneous electron donation and withdrawal on the same radical center (captodative effect) provides extra stabilization. (B) True: Chlorine lone-pair $\pi$-donation stabilizes the vacant $p$-orbital of singlet $:\text{CCl}_2$, making the singlet its ground state. (C) False: The methyl radical ($^{\bullet}\text{CH}_3$) is planar (trigonal planar, $D_{3h}$, $\text{H}-\text{C}-\text{H} = 120^\circ$, with the unpaired electron in a $2p$ orbital). (D) True: Acylium ions are linear ($sp$ carbon) with major resonance contributor $\text{R}-\text{C}\equiv\text{O}^+$. Hence, (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of gauche-butane interactions present in the lowest-energy chair conformation of *cis*-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: In either degenerate chair conformation of *cis*-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane, one methyl group is axial and the other is equatorial. The axial methyl group experiences $2$ gauche-butane interactions with the ring $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds (at C3 and C5), the equatorial methyl experiences $0$ gauche interactions with the ring, and the two adjacent methyl groups (one axial, one equatorial) are gauche ($60^\circ$) to each other ($1$ additional interaction). Total gauche-butane interactions $= 2 + 0 + 1 = 3$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: If the zero-point energy difference between a $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond and a $\text{C}-\text{D}$ bond is $\Delta\text{ZPE} = 4.80\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and the bond is completely broken (zero force constant) in the transition state, the theoretical maximum primary kinetic isotope effect ($k_H / k_D$) at $300\text{ K}$ is _____ (rounded off to two decimal places). [Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: When the $\text{C}-\text{H}/\text{C}-\text{D}$ stretching vibration is completely lost in the transition state, the difference in activation energy is $\Delta E_a = \Delta\text{ZPE} = 4800\text{ J mol}^{-1}$. Thus, $\frac{k_H}{k_D} = \exp\left(\frac{\Delta\text{ZPE}}{RT}\right) = \exp\left(\frac{4800}{8.314 \times 300}\right) = \exp(1.9245) = 6.85$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Viewed along the $\text{C1} \to \text{C3}$ axis, an enantiomer of 1,3-diphenylpropa-1,2-diene has the front C1 substituents $-\text{Ph}$ pointing UP (12 o'clock) and $-\text{H}$ pointing DOWN (6 o'clock), while the rear C3 substituents have $-\text{Ph}$ pointing RIGHT (3 o'clock) and $-\text{H}$ pointing LEFT (9 o'clock). Its correct axial stereochemical descriptors are:
optionsEn: $(R_a)$ and $(M)$
$(S_a)$ and $(P)$
$(R_a)$ and $(P)$
$(S_a)$ and $(M)$
questions.explanationEn: Using the CIP axial chirality rules along the $\text{C1} \to \text{C3}$ axis: front groups take priorities 1 and 2 (front $-\text{Ph} = 1$ at 12 o'clock; front $-\text{H} = 2$ at 6 o'clock), and rear groups take priorities 3 and 4 (rear $-\text{Ph} = 3$ at 3 o'clock; rear $-\text{H} = 4$ at 9 o'clock). Tracing $1 \to 2 \to 3$ (12 $\to$ 6 $\to$ 3 o'clock) proceeds counter-clockwise, giving $(S_a)$. By the helicity rule, the shortest dihedral angle from front senior group (12 o'clock) to rear senior group (3 o'clock) is $+90^\circ$ clockwise, giving $(P)$. Thus, the descriptors are $(S_a)$ and $(P)$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the chelation-controlled (Cram-chelate) addition of $\text{Me}_2\text{Zn}$ in the presence of $\text{TiCl}_4$ to $(2S)$-2-(benzyloxy)propanal ($\text{BnO}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHO}$). Compared to the non-chelated Felkin-Anh addition of $\text{MeLi}$ in THF/HMPA, the major products obtained are:
optionsEn: Chelation gives *syn*-3-(benzyloxy)butan-2-ol; Felkin-Anh gives *anti*-3-(benzyloxy)butan-2-ol
Chelation gives *anti*-3-(benzyloxy)butan-2-ol; Felkin-Anh gives *syn*-3-(benzyloxy)butan-2-ol
Both pathways give *syn*-3-(benzyloxy)butan-2-ol
Both pathways give *anti*-3-(benzyloxy)butan-2-ol
questions.explanationEn: With the strong bidentate Lewis acid $\text{TiCl}_4$, the aldehyde oxygen and the $\alpha$-$-\text{OBn}$ oxygen form a rigid 5-membered chelate ring. Attack of the methyl nucleophile occurs from the less hindered face opposite the C2 methyl group (past $-\text{H}$), placing $-\text{OH}$ and $-\text{OBn}$ on the same side in the zigzag representation (*syn*-3-(benzyloxy)butan-2-ol, $(2S,3S)$). Under non-chelating Felkin-Anh conditions (Polar Felkin-Anh / Cornforth model), the electronegative $-\text{OBn}$ group is placed perpendicular to $\text{C}=\text{O}$ (to maximize $\sigma^*_{\text{C}-\text{O}}$ overlap), and nucleophilic attack past $-\text{H}$ yields the opposite *anti*-3-(benzyloxy)butan-2-ol ($(2R,3S)$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A Hammett plot of $\log(k_X / k_H)$ versus $\sigma_X$ for the hydrolysis of substituted benzaldehydes' semicarbazones (or the reaction of substituted benzaldehydes with semicarbazide at neutral pH) exhibits a **concave-down** (downward-curving) break in slope. A concave-down Hammett plot is diagnostic of:
optionsEn: A change in the rate-determining step within the same multi-step mechanism
Two parallel competing mechanisms operating simultaneously
A concerted single-step reaction with no intermediates
An error in the measurement of $\sigma_X$
questions.explanationEn: In a consecutive two-step mechanism ($\text{A} \rightleftharpoons \text{I} \to \text{P}$), the overall rate is governed by the SLOWER step. When substituent variation causes the rate-determining step to switch from one step (with slope $\rho_1$) to the other step (with slope $\rho_2$), the observed rate is bounded from above by the slower of the two curves, producing a **concave-down** Hammett plot. (Conversely, two parallel competing pathways yield a concave-up plot because the faster pathway dominates.)

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The ratio of rates of $E2$ elimination with $\text{NaOEt}/\text{EtOH}$ for neomenthyl chloride (C1-Me equatorial, C2-Cl axial, C5-$^i\text{Pr}$ equatorial) versus menthyl chloride (C1-Me equatorial, C2-Cl equatorial, C5-$^i\text{Pr}$ equatorial) is approximately $200 : 1$. Furthermore, the major alkene products obtained from neomenthyl chloride and menthyl chloride are, respectively:
optionsEn: 3-Menthene (Zaitsev) from neomenthyl chloride and 2-menthene (Hofmann) from menthyl chloride
2-Menthene from neomenthyl chloride and 3-menthene from menthyl chloride
3-Menthene from both chlorides
2-Menthene from both chlorides
questions.explanationEn: In neomenthyl chloride, the lowest-energy chair already has $-\text{Cl}$ axial with antiperiplanar axial hydrogens at both C3 (tertiary) and C1 (secondary), so $E2$ is very fast and gives the more substituted Zaitsev alkene (3-menthene, $\sim 75\%$). In menthyl chloride, the stable chair has all three groups equatorial; to place $-\text{Cl}$ axial for $E2$, it must ring-flip to a high-energy all-axial chair (explaining the $200$-fold slower rate), where only the C1 axial hydrogen is antiperiplanar to $-\text{Cl}$, yielding exclusively 2-menthene (Hofmann product).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Thermolysis of ethyl azidoformate ($\text{EtO}_2\text{CN}_3$) in the presence of *cis*-4-methylpent-2-ene produces an aziridine with high retention of *cis* stereochemistry, whereas photosensitized decomposition (using benzophenone) yields a mixture of *cis*- and *trans*-aziridines. This occurs because:
optionsEn: Thermolysis generates a singlet nitrene ($^1\text{EtO}_2\text{C}\ddot{\text{N}}$) that adds concertedly, whereas triplet sensitization generates a triplet nitrene ($^3\text{EtO}_2\text{C}\ddot{\text{N}}$) that adds stepwise via a 1,3-diradical
Thermolysis proceeds via a carbene while photosensitization proceeds via a nitrene
Benzophenone catalyzes *cis*-to-*trans* isomerization of the alkene before nitrene addition
Triplet nitrenes add concertedly while singlet nitrenes add stepwise
questions.explanationEn: Thermal extrusion of $\text{N}_2$ from an organic azide conserves spin and yields a **singlet nitrene**, which adds concertedly and stereospecifically to alkenes to retain the *cis* geometry in the aziridine. Triplet sensitization by benzophenone promotes intersystem crossing to the **triplet nitrene**, which adds stepwise through a triplet 1,3-diradical intermediate, allowing $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond rotation before spin inversion and ring closure to give both *cis* and *trans* aziridines.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the molecule $(1R,2S)$-1,2-dibromo-1,2-diphenylethane (*meso*-stilbene dibromide). Which of the following statements are CORRECT?
optionsEn: Its anti-periplanar conformer (with both $-\text{Ph}$ groups anti and both $-\text{Br}$ groups anti) possesses a center of inversion ($i$)
Its fully eclipsed conformer (with $-\text{Ph}$ eclipsing $-\text{Ph}$ and $-\text{Br}$ eclipsing $-\text{Br}$) possesses a plane of symmetry ($\sigma$)
Treatment with $\text{NaI}$ in acetone (concerted anti-debromination) yields exclusively $(E)$-stilbene
Treatment with $\text{NaI}$ in acetone yields exclusively $(Z)$-stilbene
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: In *meso*-1,2-dibromo-1,2-diphenylethane, placing both $-\text{Ph}$, both $-\text{Br}$, and both $-\text{H}$ antiperiplanar generates an exact center of inversion ($i$, point group $C_i$). (B) True: Rotating one carbon by $180^\circ$ eclipses identical groups, creating a mirror plane ($\sigma$, point group $C_s$). (C) True & (D) False: $\text{I}^-$-mediated debromination is a stereospecific *anti*-elimination; in the antiperiplanar $\text{Br}-\text{C}-\text{C}-\text{Br}$ conformer of the *meso* isomer, the two $-\text{Ph}$ groups are *trans* (anti) to each other, yielding exclusively $(E)$-stilbene. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about elimination mechanisms ($E1$, $E2$, $E1\text{cb}$) are CORRECT?
optionsEn: In a concerted $E2$ reaction, switching from a good leaving group ($-\text{Br}$) to a poor, positively charged leaving group ($-\text{NMe}_3^+$) shifts the transition state toward more carbanion-like ($E1\text{cb}$-like) character and favors the Hofmann alkene
In the $E1\text{cb}_{\text{rev}}$ mechanism, the rate law is first-order in substrate and first-order in base (overall second-order), identical in kinetic form to $E2$

A large leaving-group kinetic isotope effect (e.g., $^{32}\text{S}/^{34}\text{S}$ or $^{12}\text{C}-\text{Br}$ cleavage) is absent in an $E1\text{cb}_{\text{irr}}$ mechanism where deprotonation is rate-determining
Bredt's rule permits rapid $E2$ formation of a bridgehead double bond in bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane (norbornane) derivatives
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Poor/charged leaving groups like $-\text{NMe}_3^+$ acidify the $\beta$-H and resist C–N cleavage, shifting the $E2$ transition state toward $E1\text{cb}$-like character and favoring the less substituted Hofmann alkene. (B) True: In $E1\text{cb}_{\text{rev}}$, $\text{rate} = k_2 K_{\text{eq}} [\text{Substrate}][\text{B}^-]/[\text{BH}]$, which at constant $[\text{BH}]$ (solvent) is first-order in substrate and first-order in base. (C) True: If deprotonation is irreversible and rate-determining ($E1\text{cb}_{\text{irr}}$), the leaving group bond is not broken in the RDS, so no leaving-group KIE is observed. (D) False: Bredt's rule forbids bridgehead double bonds in small bridged bicyclic rings like norbornane due to severe twisting strain. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about carbocation stability and rearrangements are CORRECT?
optionsEn: In the gas phase, the *tert*-butyl cation ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$) is slightly more stable than the primary benzyl cation ($\text{PhCH}_2^+$)

Acid-catalyzed pinacol rearrangement of 2-methyl-1,1-diphenylpropane-1,2-diol ($\text{Ph}_2\text{C(OH)}-\text{C(OH)Me}_2$) proceeds via the diaryl carbocation and a 1,2-methyl shift to yield 3,3-diphenylbutan-2-one
The 2-norbornyl cation adopts a symmetric 3-center-2-electron bridged non-classical structure and undergoes nucleophilic trapping predominantly from the *exo* face
An $\alpha$-methoxy substituent strongly destabilizes an adjacent carbocation due to its $-I$ inductive effect
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Gas-phase hydride ion affinity measurements show $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$ is slightly more stable than $\text{PhCH}_2^+$ (by $\sim 2\text{--}3\text{ kcal mol}^{-1}$). (B) True: Loss of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ occurs preferentially at the diphenyl-substituted carbon to form the stabilized $\text{Ph}_2\text{C}^+$ ion, followed by a 1,2-methyl migration to give 3,3-diphenylbutan-2-one. (C) True: The bridged 3c-2e non-classical 2-norbornyl cation blocks the *endo* face, directing nucleophilic attack selectively to the *exo* face. (D) False: An $\alpha$-methoxy group powerfully *stabilizes* a carbocation through $+M$ lone-pair resonance to form an oxocarbenium ion ($\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{O}^+\text{Me}$). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers (including both optically active enantiomers and achiral *meso* forms) possible for cyclohexane-1,2,3,4,5,6-hexol (inositol) is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Enumerating all distinct relative up/down arrangements of the six $-\text{OH}$ groups on cyclohexane-1,2,3,4,5,6-hexol: (1) all-cis (cis-inositol, achiral); (2) 5-up, 1-down (epi-inositol, achiral); (3) 4-up, 2-down with the 2 down at 1,2 (allo-inositol, achiral), 1,3 (myo-inositol, achiral), or 1,4 (muco-inositol, achiral); (4) 3-up, 3-down with the 3 down at 1,2,3 (neo-inositol, achiral), 1,3,5 (scyllo-inositol, achiral), or 1,2,4 (D-chiro- and L-chiro-inositol, a chiral enantiomeric pair of $2$ isomers). Total stereoisomers $= 7\text{ achiral} + 2\text{ chiral} = 9$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of **optically active** (chiral) stereoisomers possible for 2,3,4,5-tetrachlorohexane is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: 2,3,4,5-Tetrachlorohexane is a symmetric molecule with $n = 4$ (even) stereocenters. By the standard stereoisomer formula for symmetric molecules with even $n$, the number of optically active (chiral) isomers is $2^{n-1} = 2^{4-1} = 8$ (forming $4$ enantiomeric pairs), while the number of achiral *meso* isomers is $2^{(n/2)-1} = 2^1 = 2$, namely $(2R,3R,4S,5S)$ and $(2R,3S,4R,5S)$. Thus, there are $8$ optically active stereoisomers.
